name: My Very Best Vanilla Cake
rw:massLossNote: Baking drives off moisture. The source's own '~560 g per pan' for two pans (1120 g) against ~1218 g of batter implies roughly 8%.
rw:vesselNote: Capacity is the source's own '~560 g per pan'. Only consulted when the recipe is scaled — doubling gives ~2.2 kg of batter against 1.12 kg of tin.

rw:storage.rw:qualityNote: stays properly moist for 4 days; still good on day 7 but drier
rw:storage.rw:condition: unless the climate is very hot

rw:storageConflictNote: The buttercream component says 'keep covered in the fridge, and frosted cakes stay in the fridge'. This recipe says room temperature is better than refrigerated. That is a direct contradiction between a component and its parent, so the parent's storage is declared authoritative rather than intersected. The validator still reports the conflict — silently picking one is what makes a component with raw egg dangerous.
recipeIngredient: 4 large eggs (50-55g each), at room temperature
115g (1/2 cup/1 stick) unsalted butter, cut into cubes

rw:ingredients.rw:note: Leavening does not scale linearly with batter mass; pan depth matters more than total volume.
Volume measures of salt are not portable between brands — Diamond Crystal is about half the mass per spoon of Morton.

rw:requiredState.rw:procedure: Fridge-cold eggs can be warmed in warm tap water for 5 minutes.

rw:ingredients.rw:originalText: 4 large eggs (50-55g/2 oz each), at room temperature
115g (1/2 cup/1 stick) unsalted butter, cut into cubes
rw:ingredients.rw:note: Same food as the frosting's butter, different required state — melted here, softened there. They merge on a shopping list and must not merge in mise en place.
The source gives 240 ml for '1 cup', which is the US cup, while its dry cups match the 250 ml Australian cup. Recorded in millilitres so the system setting cannot re-interpret it.
The source explicitly says do not increase this quantity.

rw:components.rw:label: Vanilla buttercream
rw:components.rw:presentationNote: Inline rather than linked, because this recipe insists its components are not made ahead — but see makeAhead below, which contradicts that for the frosting specifically.
rw:components.rw:requiresNote: The cake never states how much frosting it uses — step 22 only says 'frost between layers and on top and sides'. One batch is what the source means, and doubling the cake doubles this with no geometry involved.

rw:makeAhead.rw:stateAtUse: brought to room temperature and beaten on low to re-fluff

rw:adjustments.rw:note: This page states 225 g where the standalone recipe states 250 g, both called '2 sticks' (which is really 226.8 g). That moves the butter:sugar ratio from 1:2.0 to 1:2.22, which is a real difference in stiffness, not rounding noise. Recorded as a local override rather than resolved.

rw:components.rw:adjustmentProvenance: importer — asserted from the parent page, not confirmed by a human. Whether this is a genuine variant or an editing artefact cannot be decided from the data.
rw:alternativeFinishes: jam and cream, Victoria Sponge style
rw:components.rw:alternativesNote: Step 22 offers six mutually exclusive finishes. The dataflow graph is pure AND, so a genuine choice point is not yet expressible; these are carried as text until an OR node exists.

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat oven to 180C/350F (160C fan). Position shelf in middle of oven.
Grease 2 x 20cm (8") cake pans with butter and line with parchment/baking paper.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a large bowl. Set aside.
Beat eggs for 30 seconds on speed 6 of a stand mixer with whisk attachment.

rw:leadBefore.rw:reason: the source requires the oven preheated 20 minutes before the batter is started

recipeInstructions.text: With beater running, pour sugar in over 45 seconds.
Beat for 7 minutes on speed 8 until tripled in volume and white/pale.
While eggs are beating, place butter and milk in a heatproof jug. Microwave on high for 2 minutes to melt butter (or use stovetop).
Add flour in 3 batches to egg mixture, beating for 5 seconds on speed 1 between each addition. After final addition, beat for 5-10 seconds until no flour is visible, then stop immediately.
Pour hot milk, vanilla extract, and oil into the now-empty flour bowl.

rw:maxDelayAfter.rw:reason: keeps the melted butter and milk hot; this is why the source melts them while the eggs beat rather than up front

recipeInstructions.text: Add approximately 1 1/2 cups (2 ladles) of cake batter to the hot milk. Whisk vigorously until smooth and foamy.
recipeInstructions.rw:portionNote: Found by the portion validator: this step and the next both consumed the whole batter, which cannot both be true. The tempering takes a couple of ladles and the rest goes back in afterwards.

rw:maxDelayAfter.rw:reason: the source requires the milk and butter to still be hot when incorporated; left standing they go cold

recipeInstructions.text: Turn beater to speed 1. Slowly pour the hot milk mixture into the cake batter over 15 seconds, then turn beater off.
Scrape down bowl sides and base. Beat on speed 1 for 10 seconds until batter is smooth and pourable.
recipeInstructions.rw:doneness: the batter is smooth and pourable

recipeInstructions.text: Pour batter evenly into prepared pans (approximately 560g/20 oz per pan).

rw:maxDelayAfter.rw:reason: air bubbles subside quickly once mixing stops; a batter left sitting bakes dense

recipeInstructions.text: Bang each pan on counter 3 times to knock out large air bubbles.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the centre comes out clean.
recipeInstructions.rw:doneness: golden brown, and a toothpick in the centre comes out clean
recipeInstructions.rw:donenessNote: The 30 minutes is the 2 x 20cm entry of rw:bakeTimeByVessel below, and the state is what decides. Both halves matter here for the same reason: the time is a property of the tin and the doneness is a property of the cake.

rw:maxDelayAfter.rw:reason: the batter must go straight into a preheated oven

rw:bakeTimeByVessel.rw:note: see the separate Vanilla Cupcakes recipe

recipeInstructions.rw:bakeTimeNote: A lookup, deliberately not interpolated. Bake time is not a function of batch mass — 3 shallower 20 cm layers take 22 minutes where 2 deeper ones take 30.

recipeInstructions.text: Remove from oven. Cool in pans for 15 minutes.
Gently turn out onto cooling racks. For level layers, cool upside down; the slight dome flattens as the cake cools.
Once cake layers are fully cool, frost between the layers and on the top and sides with the vanilla buttercream.

rw:notes: Read the recipe fully before beginning.
Verify baking powder is fresh and active.
Follow the steps in order; do not prepare components ahead.
Do not leave batter sitting once mixing begins; air bubbles subside quickly, resulting in a dense cake.
Ensure milk and butter are hot when incorporated.
Keep the mixing bowl at room temperature, not cold.
Do not add inclusions like sprinkles or blueberries; they sink.
